What this means for your system

  • Your daily energy need drives the panel and battery size.
  • The peak simultaneous wattage sets the minimum inverter size.

NEC 690 Reference Charts

Solar panel circuits follow NEC Article 690, not Article 210. These charts are reference only. A licensed electrician must verify all wiring and overcurrent protection before power is turned on.

NEC 690.8 — Panel Current Sizing

Panel current is multiplied by 1.25 twice (1.25 × 1.25 = 1.56x) for conductor and overcurrent protection sizing. Use DC-rated devices.

Panel Current (A)Continuous (×1.25)Double-Count (×1.56)Wire Ampacity (min)Fuse/Breaker Rating
1012.515.618 AWG (16A)20A DC-rated
202531.214 AWG (25A)35A DC-rated
3037.546.812 AWG (30A)50A DC-rated
405062.410 AWG (40A)70A DC-rated
607593.68 AWG (50A)100A DC-rated

NEC 690.14 — Overcurrent Protection

Fuses and breakers must be rated for DC circuits and listed for photovoltaic systems. Standard copper wire ampacity per NEC Table 310.16 (75°C column) applies to the *wire*, but the *fuse/breaker* must be DC-rated.

Wire Size (AWG)Copper Ampacity (75°C)Max Continuous Load (÷1.56)Fusion/Breaker

12 AWG30A19A25A DC-rated
10 AWG35A22A30A DC-rated

How to use

  1. Type an appliance's name, its wattage, and how many hours you use it each day.
  2. Click Add to log it.
  3. The table totals your daily watt-hours and shows system recommendations.
  4. Use Print Worksheet to keep a copy for your build.

This is a planning tool only. Verify all wattage labels and local electrical codes before wiring.
